title: Input
description: Q3 YAML input manifest — the user-facing input file format read by YAMLInputParser (src/io/input/parser/yaml.hpp). Every object here that Q3 owns end to end is closed (additionalProperties: false); those key sets are code-generated into src/generated/q3/input.hpp and are what the parser rejects unknown keys against, so this file is the single source of truth for which keys a manifest may contain.

self_consistent_field.title: Input method scf
self_consistent_field.description: SCF settings. Spelled either 'scf' or 'self_consistent_field'; both are the same block. The abbreviation 'nspin' is deliberately absent — the parser rejects it and points at number_of_spin_components.

diagonalization.description: Eigensolver: 'davidson' (iterative) or 'direct' (dense LAPACK; incompatible with DFT+U)

basis_expansion_factor.description: Davidson working basis size as a multiple of the band count. The solver holds two arrays of this many vectors, so it is the dominant term in its memory. Defaults to 2; 4 restarts less often at twice the footprint, and was the default before 2026-09-13. A non-self-consistent run uses 4 unless this is set: a single pass at 2 can return a spectrum with an eigenvalue missing, so setting it lower there is a memory choice the run warns about.

number_of_bands.description: Number of Kohn-Sham states to compute. 0 = auto-determined from electrons + empty states

total_charge.description: Net cell charge in electrons removed (QE tot_charge convention): positive = cationic (electrons removed), negative = anionic (electrons added)

number_of_spin_components.description: Number of spin components: 1 = unpolarized, 2 = collinear spin-polarized (LSDA)

starting_magnetization.description: Initial magnetization per species, keyed by the species symbol as written in the material basis (so Fe1/Fe2 AFM sublattices are separable). QE convention: values in [-1, 1], negative = opposite sublattice

atomic_starting_magnetization.description: Initial magnetization per atom, one value per atom of the material basis in order (QE convention, [-1, 1]). Lets atoms of one species start antiparallel (same-species antiferromagnet). Exclusive with starting_magnetization

type.description: Occupation smearing scheme, with QE's aliases: none/fixed (step function), gaussian, methfessel-paxton, marzari-vanderbilt (cold), fermi-dirac

order.description: Hermite expansion order N of Methfessel-Paxton smearing (Phys. Rev. B 40, 3616); valid only with a Methfessel-Paxton type

mode.description: Density mixing algorithm: 'broyden' (G-space quasi-Newton), 'linear' (plain G-space), or 'anderson' (real-space Pulay/DIIS)

beta.description: Mixing parameter (0 = no mixing, 1 = full replacement)

ndim.description: Number of previous iterations kept for Broyden/Anderson mixing

preconditioning.description: Density mixing preconditioning. 'default' resolves to 'kerker' when smearing is enabled and 'none' otherwise

q0.description: Thomas-Fermi screening wavevector for Kerker preconditioning, in inverse bohr

hubbard.description: DFT+U (Dudarev) corrections per species/orbital shell. Empty = no Hubbard correction

species.description: Element symbol matching a species label in the material basis

orbital_label.description: Orbital shell label (e.g. '3d', 'D', '4f') matching a UPF PP_CHI label, or a bare orbital letter selecting on angular momentum

u_ev.description: Hubbard U parameter in electron volts (converted to Rydberg internally)

hubbard_projectors.description: Projector convention: 'atomic' (raw pseudo-atomic UPF orbitals, QE HUBBARD {atomic}) or 'ortho-atomic' (Lowdin-orthogonalized, QE HUBBARD {ortho-atomic})

hubbard_starting_eigenvalues.description: First-iteration occupation-eigenvalue overrides (QE starting_ns_eigenvalue analog). Empty = no seeding

items.title: Input method scf hubbard starting eigenvalue

species.description: Species symbol, matched as written in the structure

hubbard_fixed_occupation_iterations.description: SCF iterations for which the seeded occupation matrix is re-imposed (QE mixing_fixed_ns). 0 = seed the first iteration only

shifts.description: K-point grid shifts [s1, s2, s3], each 0 or 1

material.description: Crystal structure: either a path to an external ESSE material JSON (resolved relative to the manifest's directory) or an inline map of the same shape. Deliberately not a closed object — an ESSE material legitimately carries fields Q3 does not consume

oneOf.description: Path to an external ESSE material JSON file

type.description: Lattice type, upper-cased on parse. 'FCC', 'BCC', 'SC' and 'CUB' take the Bravais-index construction; any other value (e.g. 'HEX', 'TRI', 'ORT') is built from the a/b/c/alpha/beta/gamma cell parameters, with gamma defaulting to 120 degrees for 'HEX'

a.description: Lattice parameter a, in lattice units

b.description: Lattice parameter b, in lattice units (defaults to a)

c.description: Lattice parameter c, in lattice units (defaults to a)

gamma.description: Angle gamma in degrees (120 for lattice type 'HEX')

units.description: Units for the scalar lattice fields; either a bare length unit or a {length, angle} map. Default 'bohr'

vectors.title: Input material lattice vectors
vectors.description: Explicit lattice vectors. Takes precedence over type + a

alat.description: Scalar multiplier applied to the vector rows

units.description: Unit for the vector rows specifically; overrides lattice.units

coordinates.description: Position per site, parallel to elements

value.description: Position in crystal coordinates [x, y, z]

units.description: Accepted but not applied — inline basis coordinates are read as crystal coordinates

type.description: Model type (e.g. 'dft'). Accepted but not consumed — Kohn-Sham DFT is the only supported model

subtype.description: Model subtype (e.g. 'gga'). Accepted but not consumed

functional.description: Exchange-correlation functional, matched case-insensitively and recorded lower-cased: 'PZ' (alias 'LDA'), 'PBE', 'PBEsol', 'BLYP', 'revPBE', 'RPBE'; 'libxc:<X>:<C>' where each half is a LibXC id or a LibXC name (e.g. 'libxc:117:130' or 'libxc:gga_x_rpbe:gga_c_pbe'); or QE's 'XC-iii-jjj-kkk-lll' form. Unrecognized values throw. Omitted, the run uses the functional the pseudopotentials state, as pw.x does without input_dft; datasets that disagree, or state one Q3 does not map, are refused

dispersion.description: Semi-empirical dispersion correction, lower-cased on parse: 'd3bj' = DFT-D3 with Becke-Johnson damping

type.description: Method type (e.g. 'pseudopotential'). Accepted but not consumed — planewave-pseudopotential is the only supported method

subtype.description: Free-form dataset label (e.g. 'norm-conserving', 'ultrasoft', 'paw'). Accepted but not consumed — the actual dataset kind is read from the pseudopotential files

pseudopotentials.description: Element symbol to pseudopotential file path, resolved relative to the manifest's directory

wavefunction.description: Plane-wave kinetic energy cutoff for wavefunctions in Rydberg

density.description: Plane-wave kinetic energy cutoff for the charge density in Rydberg. 0 = auto-derived from the wavefunction cutoff

number_of_bands.description: Number of bands for a band-structure run; overrides method.scf.number_of_bands

calculation.description: Type of calculation to perform. The short spellings map to the canonical long ones on parse. 'interpolation' names an input that q3_utility interpolate evaluates from a saved model (see control.interpolation); the engine itself refuses it, as it does the Python-orchestrated band_structure/relaxation/density_of_states

verbosity.description: How much the run prints: 'default' reports the physics and the SCF trajectory, 'high' adds the per-iteration and per-phase diagnostics (Davidson micro-iterations, timing breakdowns, mixer internals). Quantum ESPRESSO's verbosity maps onto this: 'high'/'debug' select 'high', 'low'/'medium'/'minimal'/'default' select 'default'. An explicit --log-level overrides it

disable_symmetry.description: If true, use no symmetry at all: the k-point mesh is not reduced, and the density, forces and stress are not symmetrized (Quantum ESPRESSO nosym + noinv)

nonlocal_stress_derivative_method.description: Method for nonlocal stress derivatives: 'analytical' (Lagrange polynomial differentiation, matches QE) or 'numerical' (finite-difference)

number_of_kpoint_pools.description: Number of k-point pool groups for MPI parallelization. 0 = choose automatically from the irreducible k-point count. An explicit --pools flag overrides this

use_deterministic_fft_planning.description: If true, use FFTW_ESTIMATE for bit-reproducible runs at a performance cost. If false (default), use FFTW_MEASURE

use_exact_wavefunction_grid.description: If true, size the wavefunction FFT grid exactly, for 4 x ecutwfc as pw.x does, at 1.4-2.3x the solver time on the silicon and copper examples. If false (default), use the 2 x ecutwfc grid: faster, but V(r)psi(r) and the band density alias, which costs up to mRy against pw.x on hard pseudopotentials at low cutoffs. QE-format input always uses the exact grid

isolated_system_correction.description: Isolated (charged) system correction: 'makov-payne' (QE assume_isolated='makov-payne', cubic lattices only) or 'martyna-tuckerman' (post-SCF evaluation, any lattice)

mean_field_export.description: Mean-field export for many-body perturbation theory: 'berkeleygw' writes WFN/RHO/vxc.dat

band_path.description: High-symmetry path for band-structure calculations. Each entry is either a bare label or a {label, coordinates} map

oneOf.description: High-symmetry point label looked up internally (e.g. 'Gamma', 'X', 'L')

coordinates.description: Explicit crystal coordinates [kx, ky, kz], overriding the internal label lookup

band_path_points_per_segment.description: Number of k-points sampled per band-path segment

kpoints_list.description: Explicit k-point list for NSCF calculations. Takes precedence over method.scf.kgrid when non-empty

items.description: [kx, ky, kz, weight] — crystal coordinates plus an unnormalized weight

dos_broadening.description: Gaussian broadening for the density of states in Rydberg

dos_energy_min.description: DOS energy range lower bound in Rydberg. Set to 0 to auto-determine from band energies

dos_energy_max.description: DOS energy range upper bound in Rydberg. Set to 0 to auto-determine from band energies

dos_energy_steps.description: Number of energy grid points for the DOS

compute_projections.description: Compute atomic-orbital (ortho-atomic/Lowdin) projections during an NSCF run. Opt-in: adds a Lowdin pass per k-point

interpolation.title: Input control interpolation
interpolation.description: Band-structure interpolation from a small model built out of a finished calculation. On an NSCF run (calculation: nscf) the block asks the engine to build the model and save it as <prefix>.save/interpolation.q3ip; on calculation: interpolation it names the saved model that q3_utility interpolate evaluates along control.band_path / control.kpoints_list and on dos_mesh. Each key belongs to exactly one of those two steps and is REFUSED on the other rather than ignored: grid, bands, projection_centers, projection_decay_bohr and export_formats are read when the record is captured, because they decide what goes into it; dos_mesh, disentanglement, localization, projectability_minimum, projectability_maximum and frozen_window_above_fermi_ev are read when the model is evaluated, because the record deliberately stores the untouched window so one capture serves several answers. method is given on both

method.description: How the model is built. 'wannier': Wannier functions in the one-shot projection gauge from the interface matrices of a full-grid NSCF run

grid.description: [n1, n2, n3], the full, unreduced k-point grid control.kpoints_list enumerates. Required on the NSCF build step, and stated explicitly because an explicit k-point list carries no grid shape of its own

bands.description: [first, last], the 1-based inclusive band range the model is built from. Absent means the lowest bands, which is what an isolated valence manifold needs. Give a range when the manifold does not start at band 1 -- a pseudopotential carrying semicore states puts them below it. The range must hold exactly as many bands as there are trial orbitals, and the run must compute at least 'last' bands

disentanglement.description: How the N states the gauge is built from are chosen out of the band window. 'none' requires the window to be exactly those N states, which is what an isolated manifold gives. 'projectability' classifies every band by its projectability and energy and then chooses the smoothest subspace across the zone, which is what an entangled manifold -- a transition metal's d and s bands -- needs

localization.description: How the gauge inside the chosen subspace is fixed. Minimising the Marzari-Vanderbilt spread makes the Wannier functions as localised as the mesh allows, so H(R) decays quickly enough to interpolate BETWEEN the mesh points; the one-shot projection gauge is exact AT them whatever it does. 'auto' minimises when the record carries the neighbour overlaps M_mn(k,b) the spread is defined through, and keeps the projection gauge when it does not -- a record imported from another code's projections and eigenvalues alone carries none. 'maximal' demands it and makes such a record an error. 'none' always keeps the projection gauge, which is useful to isolate what localisation contributes

projectability_minimum.description: Disentanglement: a band whose projectability falls below this is discarded from the window entirely, unless the frozen energy window kept it

projectability_maximum.description: Disentanglement: a band whose projectability reaches this is frozen, kept exactly and never rotated by the optimisation

frozen_window_above_fermi_ev.description: Disentanglement: energy above the Fermi level, in electronvolts, below which a band is frozen whatever its projectability -- short of the singular-gauge rule: a band in the window whose projectability is below projectability_minimum is one the trial orbitals cannot represent, and it is excluded from the freeze and reported rather than frozen, because freezing it makes the gauge singular. Not redundant with projectability_maximum: a metal's Fermi-surface states are the least projectable ones, and discarding them leaves a hole the mesh-point round trip cannot see. 'auto', the default, applies the published 2 eV for atomic projectors to metal and insulator alike: it is the window the band distance that judges the model is measured on, and the two must coincide -- silicon at 12x12x12 gives 220 meV with the occupied manifold alone frozen and 14 meV at E_F + 2 eV, the whole difference being the lowest conduction band. For an insulator the Fermi level the engine reports sits in the gap, so the window reaches the conduction states the distance weighs and no further. Whether the system is a metal (a band crossing the Fermi level) is decided and reported either way. Any real number overrides the rule, and a value below the whole manifold freezes nothing by energy

localization_maximum_iterations.description: Evaluation step: the spread minimiser's iteration budget. Far more than a well-posed case needs (copper converges in about sixty); the retry ladder doubles it after a stall, which is the one reason it is a key

disentanglement_maximum_iterations.description: Evaluation step: the subspace iteration's budget. A disentanglement that exhausts it is an error, never a subspace returned as if it had converged; the error prints the last five gauge-invariant spreads

disentanglement_convergence_tolerance.description: Evaluation step: the relative change in the gauge-invariant spread the subspace iteration must stay below, over five iterations, to count as converged. The automatic workflow's retry ladder loosens it for a disentanglement that exhausted its budget, to a margin above the change among the spreads that failure printed

trial_shells.description: Build step: per species, the 0-based indices of the pseudo-atomic shells to use as trial orbitals, in the order the pseudopotential file lists its atomic wavefunctions. A species not named keeps every shell its pseudopotential does not mark unusable (a negative occupation, or a zero-norm radial function). Refused together with projection_centers. The automatic workflow always writes it, naming the shells its rule keeps: every occupied shell, and the empty ones that are not a second channel of an l the atom has in valence

projection_centers.description: Wannier: centres of the s-type trial orbitals, in crystal (fractional) coordinates. The count fixes the number of Wannier functions, so it must not exceed the band count. Empty falls back to the pseudopotentials' atom-centred atomic orbitals

items.description: [x, y, z] — crystal (fractional) coordinates of one trial-orbital centre

projection_decay_bohr.description: Wannier: decay length of those trial orbitals in bohr (Wannier90's zona is its reciprocal)

export_formats.description: Interoperability formats written beside the native record on the NSCF build step. 'wannier90': <prefix>.mmn/.amn/.eig/.nnkp for wannier90.x and the tools built on it

dos_mesh.description: Evaluation step: the dense uniform k-mesh the interpolated density of states is sampled on, binned with control.dos_broadening. Omit for no DOS

relax_force_threshold.description: Force convergence threshold for relaxation in Ry/bohr (max |force|)

relax_energy_threshold.description: Energy convergence threshold for relaxation in Rydberg (energy change between steps)
